title: Lena and the Choir
premise: August Ishikawa was born with a swordspeaker's gift in the one valley in the kingdom where magic cannot follow, and her oath-bound ancestors chose exile there to keep the gift dormant. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley hunting the last oath-bound line, August flees with a ragged found family: a defected hunt-captain, a choirgirl whose voice carries stolen magic, and a disgraced archivist who knows the truth about the king. August discovers the king is bound to an ancient parasite wearing his crown, and that her ancestors' oath was the binding's final lock. To free the king and end the hunt, August must break her family's oath, speak her sword's true name outside the valley where magic has never touched her, and accept that doing justice may cost her the only home she has ever known.
about_author: Beatrix Lockridge is the pen name of a former choir singer turned archivist who writes fantasy about the quiet violence of institutions. She lives near a river valley she refuses to name, and swears the acoustics there are magic.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: August's POV. Establishing life in Hollowmere, where magic cannot follow: August sharpens a sword she has never been allowed to name, and her grandmother reminds her of the oath that keeps the gift asleep. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built on restraint.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Mill
chapters.summary: August's POV. A royal crier announces the Crown's Edict of Purity: all gifted persons to be surrendered or hunted. August watches neighbors she's known all her life look at her differently. Emotional beat: the illusion of safety shattering.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her grandmother teaches her the first half of the family's true history: the oath was not protection from the gift, but a lock on something larger. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as burden.

chapters.title: The Hunt-Captain at the Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. Captain Sera Vane arrives with witch-hunters, following a map only an Ishikawa could have drawn. Grandmother sends August into the cellar tunnels. Emotional beat: betrayal from within.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: August's POV, fragmented. August watches Hollowmere burn from the ridge; her grandmother stays behind and does not come out. Emotional beat: grief as ignition, the moment retreat becomes impossible.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Sang Wrong
chapters.summary: Nell's POV, first appearance. A choirgirl named Nell is expelled from the cathedral choir because her voice makes candles gutter and grown men weep. She flees the city and collides with August on the road. Emotional beat: two outcasts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Company
chapters.summary: August's POV. August reluctantly lets Nell travel with her; Nell's stolen magic reacts to August's dormant gift in ways neither understands. Emotional beat: wary tenderness.

chapters.title: Sera Vane's Doubt
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The hunt-captain interrogates Hollowmere's survivors and finds the Ishikawa map's provenance suspicious—someone at court wanted the family found. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Disgraced royal archivist Tam Osgood, who leaked the Edict's hidden clauses, flees the capital with proof that the king's 'purity hunt' is actually a search for the last key. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Crossing at Greyford
chapters.summary: August's POV. August, Nell, and Tam converge at a river town and are nearly caught in a sweep; Sera, leading it, lets them slip away and can't explain why. Emotional beat: the found family assembling by accident.

chapters.title: The Road Turns North
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam reveals the binding: the king has been possessed for nineteen years by a crown-worn entity, and only an oath-bound swordspeaker can unmake it. Emotional beat: the quest acquires its shape and its horror.

chapters.title: First Song of the Gift
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Attacked by bounty hunters, Nell sings in panic and August's sword answers, moving with a will of its own. Both are terrified by what they felt. Emotional beat: wonder braided with fear.

chapters.title: Sera Deserts
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera burns her commission after being ordered to execute a gifted child, and rides north to find the fugitives she was meant to kill. Emotional beat: justice chosen over law.

chapters.title: The Oath's Weight
chapters.summary: August's POV. Around a fire, August confesses the oath's terms: if she speaks her sword's name outside the valley, the binding on the crown begins to unravel—and so does the seal keeping the entity from finding her. Emotional beat: the cost named aloud.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Unsworn
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The company shelters with a hidden community of unregistered gifted folk led by an old swordspeaker's widow who knew August's grandmother. Emotional beat: a glimpse of the family August might have had.

chapters.title: Nell's Stolen Voice
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell admits her magic isn't hers: the choirmaster fed choir children's voices into her to power cathedral wards. Emotional beat: rage at quiet, institutional cruelty.

chapters.title: The Widow's Warning
chapters.summary: August's POV. The widow reveals the entity's name—Vessel-of-Crowns—and warns that breaking the oath frees the king but marks August as its new candidate host. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sera Finds Them
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera catches up and is nearly killed by the company's defenses before Tam vouches for her. Uneasy trust begins. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered cautiously.

chapters.title: The King's True Letters
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam decodes the king's pre-possession correspondence: the young king knew what the crown was and wore it anyway, to keep it from worse hands. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as a sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Tollbridge
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Inquisition's elite, the Silent Order, ambushes the company; August's gift half-wakes to save Nell, burning through her restraint. Emotional beat: the oath fraying under pressure.

chapters.title: What August Heard in the Blade
chapters.summary: August's POV, intimate and strange. The sword speaks to August in her grandmother's voice, teaching her the second half of the family history: the oath was meant to be broken, once, by choice. Emotional beat: inheritance as invitation.

chapters.title: The Company Divided
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera argues they should kill the king and end the entity with him; August refuses to make a murderer of herself for the crown's convenience. The company splits into two camps. Emotional beat: found family tested by principle.

chapters.title: Nell's Choice
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell secretly begins training her voice to carry August's oath-song, knowing it may burn her stolen magic—and her—out. Emotional beat: love as sacrifice offered in secret.

chapters.title: The Capital's Gates
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The reunited company enters the capital disguised as a traveling choir, Nell's cover story. Emotional beat: tension coiled in ordinary streets.

chapters.title: The Silent Order's Trap
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Order captures Tam and uses him as bait; August must choose between the plan and the person. She chooses the person. Emotional beat: loyalty as strategy-breaking.

chapters.title: Tam's Interrogation
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tortured by the Order's inquisitor, Tam protects the company's plan by feeding them the archivist's true secret: he was the one who drew the Ishikawa map, years ago, under coercion. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into resistance.

chapters.title: Sera's Old Brothers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera confronts her former second-in-command and learns the Order serves the entity directly, not the king. Emotional beat: the enemy's face finally clear.

chapters.title: The Choir in the Catacombs
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The company finds the cathedral's buried crypt-choir: generations of children whose voices power the binding, kept singing past death. Nell recognizes her own stolen voice among them. Emotional beat: horror and grief fused.

chapters.title: The Oath Unbound
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the crypt, August formally breaks her family's oath before her sword, her grandmother's voice, and her found family as witnesses. The valley's seal shatters across the kingdom. Emotional beat: liberation that feels like loss.

chapters.title: The Entity Wakes
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Vessel-of-Crowns, freed of its lock, seizes the palace and the king's body begins to fail; the hunt becomes a purge as the entity tries to kill August before she can reach the throne room. Emotional beat: the clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Streets of Ash
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera leads the capital's hidden gifted in open rebellion to hold the streets while August runs for the palace. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, made flesh.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Redemption
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam breaks into the royal archive to find the counter-oath that can hold the entity after unbinding, and is mortally wounded securing it. Emotional beat: a life spent buying the ending.

chapters.title: The Throne Room Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. August fights through the Silent Order to the throne room and finds the king conscious for the first time in nineteen years, begging her to hurry. Emotional beat: the enemy as a dying man.

chapters.title: Nell's Last Song
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell sings the oath-song to carry August's voice into the binding, her stolen magic igniting and burning away. Emotional beat: sacrifice witnessed, not yet resolved.

chapters.title: The True Name
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. August speaks her sword's true name and unbinds the king, but the Vessel-of-Crowns leaps for her as its new host—and she offers it not resistance but her oath, re-sworn on her own terms, caging it in a willing keeper's discipline rather than a stolen crown. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—binding by consent, not conquest.

chapters.title: The King in the Ruin
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The king, freed and dying, abdicates in favor of a council that includes the unsworn; Sera is offered a generalship and refuses it. Emotional beat: power declined.

chapters.title: What Tam Left Behind
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, final chapter of his arc. Dying, Tam entrusts the counter-oath and the true histories to Nell, naming her the archive's keeper. Emotional beat: inheritance passed by choice, not blood.

chapters.title: The Voice That Remained
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell survives, her own voice finally her own, and sings the dead crypt-choir to rest. Emotional beat: mourning turned into music.

chapters.title: Home, Unsealed
chapters.summary: August's POV. August returns to the rebuilt Hollowmere, magic now able to follow her anywhere, and finds she no longer needs the valley to be safe—only to be remembered. Emotional beat: home as memory, not prison.

chapters.title: The Oath Re-Sworn
chapters.summary: August's POV, coda. August trains a new generation of swordspeakers who choose their oaths freely, with Nell's song and Sera's shield at her side. The sword rests, named at last. Emotional beat: the found family complete, the inheritance transformed.
